decisions.reason: Retaining current data during another controlled redeployment does not re-include NFTs from the earlier legacy contract or alter the rule that only finalized mints are reported.
The migration preserves existing data but does not change the requirement that owners locate NFTs from the active replacement contract or make earlier legacy NFTs discoverable.
The accepted migration approach does not change the metadata attributes, live on-chain metadata source, or exclusion of metadata from the earlier legacy contract.
Data continuity during redeployment does not change the required dashboard or wallet media rendering behavior, and it does not require rendering NFTs from the earlier legacy contract.
The source decision does not alter holder eligibility, Lit Protocol gating, or the rule that access is based on NFTs recognized by the active system.

The retained data may make the current 'fresh' replacement-contract prize-draw state obsolete, but the context says the preserved data is probably in the backend and does not establish whether on-chain prize-draw state is also retained.
The technical migration and data-retention strategy does not necessarily change any approved About-page copy or presentation requirement.
The controlled redeployment does not change the required USDC mint behavior, payment asset, or generic scope to the active replacement contract.
The migration strategy does not change the email-link authentication method, supported users, or dashboard access behavior.
The source decision concerns technical data continuity and does not entail any revision to the approved FAQ content.
Retaining data during contract redeployment does not change the badge set, icons, count, or dashboard layout.
The accepted deployment and data-retention approach does not entail any change to landing-page content, terminology, or layout.
